sources.label: W3C Media Capture Transform — MediaStreamTrackProcessor (Editor's Draft, fetched 2026-10-07)

inputs.rationale: totalFrames is a read-only attribute getter with an empty parameter list, so there is no input contract, option, default or validation rule for the page to state; its shape-table row gives only the type and the meaning of the value.

errors.rationale: Reading totalFrames returns the value of the processor's [[numTotalFrames]] slot and the cited specification defines no exception for it, so the page documents no error or failure state because there is none to document for either counter.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The counter is an aggregate integer about frames the caller already receives through readable, and the page documents no security or privacy consideration at all; the cited specification's Security and Privacy considerations section discusses MediaStreamTrackProcessor's permission-gated track sources and resource exhaustion without naming totalFrames.

inputs.rationale: discardedFrames is a read-only attribute getter with an empty parameter list, so there is no input contract, option, default or validation rule to state; the caller influences it only indirectly, by how fast it reads readable.

errors.rationale: Reading discardedFrames returns the value of the processor's [[numDiscardedFrames]] slot and the cited specification defines no exception for it, so the page documents no error or failure state because there is none to document for either counter.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The counter reports how many frames the processor dropped from a track the caller already holds, adding no data of its own, and the page documents no security or privacy consideration; the cited specification's Security and Privacy considerations section addresses track-source permissions and resource exhaustion without naming discardedFrames.

notes: B4 unit. THE PAGE CARRIED ZERO id ATTRIBUTES, so five existing headings gained ids and nothing else on the page changed: syntax (on 'shape of the API'), browser-support (on 'browser support') and see-also (on 'see also') are the three canonical ids; example (on 'example') and why-it-exists (on 'why it exists') were added because the examples dimension must resolve to a slice that actually contains a <pre><code> and the context dimension to a slice that actually states the context — the page's only code block sits under 'example' and its only context prose under 'why it exists', so without those two ids both dimensions would have had to be reported against slices that do not contain them. No id sits on a <section>, and no annotated <h2> opens a section whose first child is an <h3> (the page has no <h3> at all). NO CODE BLOCK WAS ADDED: the page already ships one <pre><code> (the getUserMedia + getReader loop that reads both counters), which is what the examples dimension maps to. Pattern matched to the sibling B4 unit v150/css-url-request-modifiers, which has the same page template. INVENTORY IS EXACTLY THE CHANGE: the two attributes the page's own shape table lists, each kind attribute, both confirmed in the cited Editor's Draft fetched 2026-10-07 as 'readonly attribute unsigned long long discardedFrames;' and 'readonly attribute unsigned long long totalFrames;' inside interface MediaStreamTrackProcessor. outOfScope is EMPTY rather than padded: the page declares no IDL block of its own, so the declared-surface rule finds no members to account for, and the interface's pre-existing members (its constructor and readable) are not part of this change and are not declared anywhere on the page. NOT-APPLICABLE DIMENSIONS AND THEIR GAPS, one line each: inputs (both counters are parameterless read-only getters, so no input contract exists), errors (the cited spec defines no exception for reading either slot, and the page documents none), securityPrivacy (the page has NO security or privacy section at all — that is a real gap in the page, recorded here rather than papered over; the cited spec's Security and Privacy considerations section covers MediaStreamTrackProcessor's permission-gated track sources and resource exhaustion without naming either counter). LIFECYCLE IS DOCUMENTED, NOT NOT-APPLICABLE, and the mapping is checkable: the #syntax slice states the counters run 'since the processor was created' and 'increase monotonically', which the cited spec backs — its constructor steps set [[numDiscardedFrames]] and [[numTotalFrames]] to 0, and handleNewFrame increments both. DIVERGENCE DRAFTED FOR THE IMPLEMENTER, NOT WRITTEN INTO THE PAGE (a worker must not author page prose): the browser-support table's Firefox and Safari cells both read Support 'Positive' / Notes 'Not yet shipped', and the at-a-glance table's 'Standards position (Firefox)' and 'Standards position (Safari)' rows both read 'Positive', while the source the page cites for both tables — ChromeStatus record 6267249280286720, fetched from its API 2026-10-07, accurate_as_of 2026-06-22 13:51:51, and identical in this repo's own _data/features-150.json snapshot — records ff_views = 5 with view text 'No signal' and safari_views = 5 with view text 'No signal', each carrying the note 'Spec PR was approved by Mozilla/WebKit https://github.com/w3c/mediacapture-transform/pull/125', which is the most likely origin of the page's 'Positive'. The compatibility dimension stays documented because the #browser-support slice does contain a populated cross-browser table; the fidelity of two of its cells is the implementer's call, and the draft is in the unit report. SECOND, SMALLER CANDIDATE DIVERGENCE, ALSO DRAFTED ONLY: the page's discardedFrames row attributes every drop to 'the readable stream was not being read fast enough', while the cited Editor's Draft allows more — after the maxBufferSize drop path it states 'At any time, the UA MAY remove any frame from processor.[[queue]] ... for example, to prevent resource exhaustion or to improve performance in certain situations. In this case, processor.[[numDiscardedFrames]] MUST be incremented accordingly.' GAP I COULD NOT CLOSE, STATED AS A GAP AND NOT AS A CLAIM: the cited Editor's Draft declares '[Exposed=DedicatedWorker]' on MediaStreamTrackProcessor with the note 'There is WG consensus that the interface should be exposed on DedicatedWorker. There is no WG consensus on whether or not the interface should not be exposed on Window.'; the page states no exposure context anywhere and its example is context-free, so I do not know whether the example runs where a reader would paste it. I tried to check Chromium's shipped IDL and got 404 at two candidate paths, so I assert nothing about Chrome's exposure set — this is recorded as undetermined, not as a divergence. OBSERVATIONS THAT ARE NOT DIVERGENCES: the page cites the Editor's Draft https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-transform/ while the ChromeStatus record's spec_link is https://www.w3.org/TR/mediacapture-transform/#track-processor-interface (same document, different edition URL); and the record's browsers.chrome.status.text still reads 'Proposed' with is_released = false, while its ship stage records desktop_first/android_first/webview_first = 150 and all_platforms = true, which is what supports the page's 'Chrome 150' and 'All platforms' cells — so those two cells were verified against the record rather than assumed. BOTH CONTRACT SOURCES ARE LINKED BY THE PAGE, exactly as the validator requires: every sourceRef used by an inventory item or a dimension resolves to one of the two URLs the page already cites, and no source was added that the page does not link. The page's conformance.json was not touched (it is immutable and its suiteHash must not move); its browser-support-section, min-sections and example-surface-present assertions are unaffected by adding id attributes.
